record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For supervised machine-learning algorithms built from matrix product states or related tensor networks, can one express the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis dimension explicitly as a function of the bond dimension?

evidence.quote: Question 13 Can one write the Rademacher complexity or the Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC)-dimension for such ML algorithms as a function of the bond dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider supervised machine-learning models whose hypothesis class consists of functions parameterized by a tensor network of fixed structure (e.g. a matrix product state / tensor train, a tensor ring, a CP or Tucker decomposition) with bond dimension (rank) D. Concretely, fix a tensor network architecture on N sites with local physical dimension d and a uniform bond dimension D, and let H_{N,d,D} denote the associated class of real-valued classifiers (or regressors) obtained by contracting an input feature embedding against the network and reading out a scalar.

Provide explicit closed-form expressions, as functions of the bond dimension D (and of N, d), for:

(a) the Vapnik–Chervonenkis dimension VC(H_{N,d,D}) of the resulting binary classifier family, and
(b) the (empirical or population) Rademacher complexity R_m(H_{N,d,D}) of the hypothesis class on samples of size m.

In particular, determine matching upper and lower bounds in D that exhibit the exact dependence of these complexity measures on the bond dimension for matrix product state classifiers and for related tensor network classifiers.
artifact.status_search_result: Khavari and Rabusseau (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.11827) derived matching upper and lower bounds on the VC-dimension and pseudo-dimension of tensor network classifiers (including MPS/tensor train, tensor ring, CP, Tucker) as functions of the bond dimension, explicitly addressing the VC-dimension part of the question. Explicit closed-form Rademacher complexity expressions in terms of bond dimension do not appear to be fully resolved in the same generality, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Lower and Upper Bounds on the VC-Dimension of Tensor Network Models
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the VC dimension of MPS classifiers as a function of bond dimension, answering an open problem listed by Cirac, Garre-Rubio and Pérez-García.
status_evidence.claim: VC-dimension part of the open problem has been resolved with matching upper and lower bounds in the bond dimension.

status_evidence.title: Lower and Upper Bounds on the Pseudo-Dimension of Tensor Network Models (NeurIPS 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bounds for arbitrary tensor network structures and matching lower bounds for CP, Tensor Train, Tensor Ring and Tucker.
status_evidence.claim: Pseudo-dimension and VC-dimension bounds are now known for common tensor network models in terms of bond dimension.
